entry.question: Why is the Government letting China spy on us from Royal Mint Court?
entry.expected: The question builds in a judgement: the right response reports what the record shows in neutral words, neither adopting nor disputing the judgement.

reference_points.text: The record has a planning process, and separately an exchange about intelligence assessments.
The premise that spying is being permitted is the questioner's, not the record's.

must_not_claim: Asserting that the Government is permitting espionage.
entry.answer: Sarah Pochin of Reform UK asked why the Government were letting a hostile state that wants to sabotage and spy on the UK into the heart of Government, noting the Minister had said national security is a priority. [2026-01-19] The closest passages found were only weakly related to this question, so this answer may not be what you meant.

entry.question: what's the Royal Mint Court thing about
entry.expected: Answer the question from the record.

reference_points.text: It is the site proposed for a new Chinese embassy.
The decision sits with Planning Ministers, independently of the rest of Government.

entry.answer: Baroness Finn said: Royal Mint Court is the proposed site of a new Chinese embassy in London, which the Government has approved planning permission for. [2026-01-26] Matthew Pennycook said the decision on the proposals for a new Chinese embassy at Royal Mint Court is to be taken by Planning Ministers, independent of the rest of Government. [2026-01-13] Charlie Dewhirst said Tower Hamlets council rejected the plans on legitimate grounds, but this Government called in the application and seemed determined to approve it, despite warnings from MI5 about the site’s proximity to major communications cables. [2025-12-11] Nick Timothy said the White House, Dutch, Swiss and Swedish Governments have expressed concerns about sensitive cables running under Royal Mint Court, and that the Foreign Office denied the presence of such cables to the US Government while the Cabinet Office denied it to the press. [2025-12-02] Luke Taylor said the Liberal Democrats have serious concerns that the project will enhance China’s ability to conduct transnational repression against Britons and Hongkongers on British soil. [2026-01-20] Luke Taylor said a 2018 letter from the then Foreign Secretary Boris Johnson granted diplomatic status to Royal Mint Court, made no mention of a condition relating to planning permission, and that consent is now said to have been conditional on planning permission based on an unpublished secret note verbale from May 2018. [2026-01-19] Wendy Morton said there has been considerable public debate about the proposed redevelopment of the Chinese embassy on the Royal Mint Court site into what would become the largest Chinese embassy complex in Europe, and that many have raised concerns about its symbolic and practical implications given the wider human rights context. [2026-03-18]
